title: Per-request kernel lifecycle cohorting and telemetry policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a lightweight, policy-driven telemetry layer that cohorts requests by observed kernel selection lifecycle and attention-pathway characteristics, and emits span + per-kernel metrics with deterministic naming so we can build heatmaps and cohort-based SLOs. Goal is to get actionable per-request kernel attribution while keeping overhead <1% P50 CPU and <2% GPU overhead in steady state.
acceptance_criteria: Stable NVTX + tracing naming conventions documented and applied to all kernel launches (prefill vs decode) and attention paths
Per-request cohort id is attached to top-level trace and is queryable in traces/logs/dashboards
Sampling policy implemented: error/full traces (100%), cohort-based stratified sampling for successes (configurable rates per cohort), and periodic heatmap aggregation across cohorts

Exporter mapping: per-kernel exec_time_ms, queuing_ms, memory_alloc_bytes, launch_overhead_ms exported to Prometheus with labels kernel_name,kernel_variant,model_variant,attention_path,batch_size,cohort
New dashboards (kernel heatmap by cohort/seq_len; kernel hotpath waterfall) exist in Grafana and show reasonable signal on canary workloads
End-to-end test harness validates correctness for short/long seqs, kv-cache hits, quantized kernels and shows <1% runtime overhead for sampling default rates
tasks: Design: finalize cohorting keys and sampling tiers (Aisha)
Runtime: add kernel lifecycle hooks + deterministic span names + cohort tag (Liam)
Scheduler: emit batch-level metadata (batch_size, effective_seq_len) into request context
Tracing: map NVTX ranges to span names and enrich with kernel labels (Daniel)
Metrics: expose per-kernel Prometheus metrics with labels and cardinality limits
Dashboard: Grafana panels for cohort heatmaps, per-kernel p50/p95 latency and memory
E2E: synthetic perf job and regression test in CI with sampling enabled
Rollout: canary on dedicated pool -> monitor cost/latency -> full rollout
telemetry_schema: Naming conventions: span.name = runtime.kernel.<phase>.<kernel_family>.<kernel_variant> where phase in {prefill,decode}, kernel_family e.g. attention,matmul,softmax; span.tags: {kernel_id, kernel_variant, attention_path, batch_size, seq_len, kv_cache_hit, model_variant, cohort_id}. Prometheus metrics: runtime_kernel_exec_time_ms{kernel_family,kernel_variant,model_variant,attention_path,cohort_id,batch_size=~"\d+"}. Aggregation knobs: cohort rollup at 1m and 5m windows. Trace sampling: errors=100%, cohorts: default 1% successful traces, heavy cohorts 5%, critical customers configurable per-project.
instrumentation_steps: Add request.cohort_id generator in request context: deterministic hashing of (model_variant, seq_len_bucket, attention_path_hint, quantization_profile)
Wrap each kernel launch with start_kernel_span() and end_kernel_span() which also push NVTX ranges for GPU kernels
Attach kernel lifecycle events (queued,start,end,failed) as span events and increment per-request counters
Ensure prefill vs decode flows are marked by top-level phase tag and by prefixing NVTX ranges: prefill::<kernel> and decode::<kernel>
Implement a sampling controller module that consults cohort config and marks traces for full capture or probabilistic pass-through
Export metrics via existing runtime metrics pipeline; keep label cardinality bounded by bucketing seq_len and batch_size
rollout_plan: 1) Merge runtime + tracing + metrics changes behind a feature flag. 2) Canary to 5% of traffic on a dedicated pool with sampling at conservative rates. 3) Run 48h perf and correctness suite; monitor overhead, heatmap signal, and customer-facing latencies. 4) Iterate sampling rates and cohort definitions based on signal quality. 5) Ramp to 100% after two successful canaries and signoff from SRE and PM.
qa_plan: Run synthetic suite with controlled mixes: short seq (32), medium (256), long (2048) and attention variants (sparse, local, global)
Verify cohorts receive expected traces at configured sampling rates (statistical tests over 1h windows)
Confirm span/metric label consistency between traces and Prometheus metrics for top 10 kernels
Performance regression: assert <1% CPU increase and <2% GPU time increase for sampling_on_default in steady state
Failure modes: simulate kernel timeouts and verify full traces captured and linked to cohort dashboards
